  "title": "Philippine passport: requirements (part 1 of 2)",
  "content": "- Book a confirmed online appointment at passport.gov.ph. Appointments made anywhere else are not legitimate. [1] [7]\n- Print the application form and e-receipt generated after booking and payment. [1]\n- New adult applicants: bring your PSA birth certificate on security paper (original and photocopy). Pag-IBIG, TIN and PhilHealth IDs are not accepted. [5] [1]\n- Renewing: bring your current ePassport with a photocopy of the data page. [3]\n- Married women using the spouse's surname: bring your PSA marriage certificate. You do not need it if you keep your maiden name.   "category": "services",
  "title": "Philippine passport: steps",
  "content": "1. Go to passport.gov.ph and choose Schedule an Appointment. [6]\n2. Pick the DFA consular office or Temporary Off-site Passport Services (TOPS) site, date and time. [1]\n3. Fill in the online form exactly as your PSA documents read. Major errors can lead to rejection. [1]\n4. Pay the processing fee (₱950 regular or ₱1,200 expedited) through an accredited payment channel. Fees are non-refundable and non-transferable. [1] [6]\n5. Print the confirmation, application form and receipt from your email. If no email arrives within 24 hours of paying, call (02) 8234-3488. [1]\n6. Arrive on your appointment date with your originals and photocopies.\n7. Have your photo, fingerprints and signature captured at the consular office. [1]\n8. Keep your official receipt. It shows the tentative release date. [1]\n9. Claim the passport at the same office where you applied, or wait for courier delivery if you chose it. [1]\n10. Check every detail on the data page before you leave. [1]\nSource: https://passport.gov.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).",

  "title": "Philippine passport: after you apply",
  "content": "- Validity: 10 years if you were 18 or older when you applied, 5 years if you were under 18. [7] [1]\n- Someone else claiming: an immediate family member needs an authorisation letter. Anyone else needs a Special Power of Attorney (SPA). DFA suggests renewing within one year of expiry. There is no penalty for renewing an expired passport. Most countries need at least six months of validity for travel. [1]\n- Old visas stay valid in your old passport. Carry both passports. [1]\n- Do not buy plane tickets until you have the passport in hand.   "title": "Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): do you need to file at all?",
  "content": "You do not need to file Form 1700 if any of these apply (RR 4-2024):\n- Your taxable compensation income is ₱250,000 or less.\n- You had only one employer for the whole year and it withheld your tax correctly. This is \"substituted filing\": your employer's BIR Form 2316 stands in for your return.\n- All of your income was already subject to final tax.\n- You are a minimum wage earner.\n- You are an overseas Filipino worker (OFW) for your income earned abroad.\nYou must file if you worked for two or more employers during the year, at the same time or one after another. RR 4-2024 says such earners \"are not qualified for substituted filing\" (RR 4-2024).\nWhat is BIR Form 2316? It is the Certificate of Compensation Payment/Tax Withheld that your employer gives you. It shows what you earned and how much tax was withheld. Under substituted filing, it serves as your return.  {
  "id": "bg-guide-bir-1701-which-rate-are-you-on",
  "category": "services",
  "title": "BIR Form 1701A: which rate are you on?",
  "content": "- 8% flat rate: Only available if your gross sales/receipts plus other non-operating income do not exceed the ₱3,000,000 VAT threshold, and you are not VAT-registered (RR 8-2018).\n- Choosing it: You must elect the 8% rate in your first-quarter income or percentage tax return, or in the first quarterly return after you start your business. Otherwise you are placed on graduated rates. The choice cannot be changed for that year (RR 8-2018).\n- If you pass ₱3M during the year: You automatically move to graduated rates for the whole year. Your 8% quarterly payments are credited (RR 8-2018).\n- Graduated rates + OSD: You deduct a flat 40% of gross sales/receipts instead of listing expenses (TRAIN Sec. 34(L)). You then pay graduated income tax plus 3% percentage tax if you are non-VAT (TRAIN Sec. 116).\n- Micro and small taxpayers (gross sales below ₱3M is \"micro\") may instead use the simplified Form 1701-MS. It was added to eBIRForms v7.9.6.0 (RR 8-2024; RMC 20-2026; RMC 36-2026).\nSource: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RR%20No.%208-2018.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).",

  "category": "services",
  "title": "VAT registration: what changes for your invoices and books",
  "content": "- Invoices replace official receipts. Under EOPT, the \"Invoice\" is now the main sales document for both goods and services. An Official Receipt is only a supplementary document (RR 7-2024).\n- Services are taxed on gross sales. VAT on services is now based on \"gross sales\", the same as goods, rather than on cash received (RR 3-2024).\n- No more monthly 2550M. VAT returns are quarterly only, starting 1 January 2023. This change came from the TRAIN law, not EOPT (RA 10963 Sec. 114).\n- Threshold will be updated. The ₱3M threshold is adjusted for inflation every 3 years (EOPT Sec. 109(CC); RR 3-2024). Check current BIR issuances when determining whether you must register.\nSource: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%207-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).",

  "category": "services",
  "title": "VAT registration: deadlines and penalties",
  "content": "- If you should have registered but didn't: You must pay VAT as if registered, but you cannot claim input tax credits for that period (EOPT Sec. 236(F)(2)).\n- Registration deadline: Contact your RDO as soon as your sales reach the registration threshold to confirm when you must file your registration update.\n- Late filing or payment:\n\t- 25% surcharge (NIRC Sec. 248).\n\t- 12% a year interest (TRAIN Sec. 249).\n\t- Micro and small taxpayers pay a reduced 10% surcharge and 6% interest instead (RR 6-2024).\n- Cancelling VAT registration: Possible if you expect sales over the next 12 months to stay at or below the threshold, or if you close the business. If SEC sends a compliance notice, correct the data and resubmit (SEC eSPARC).\n5. Pay the fees on the Payment Assessment Form through eSPAYSEC or Landbank over the counter (SEC eSPARC).\n6. Receive your Certificate of Incorporation.\n7. Send two hard copies of the signed and notarized documents with your proof of payment to SEC by courier or registered mail. Do this within 60 calendar days of the approval date on the certificate (SEC eSPARC).\n8.
